title: Mid-chunk code fences leak code text to TTS
reasoning: When text mode sees a code marker mid-chunk, it enters code suppression but recursively reprocesses post_marker including the opening ``` marker. The suppression branch then finds that marker at index 0 and treats it as the closing fence, immediately exits suppression, and processes the code body as normal text. For a chunk like 'text ```secret``` done', 'secret' is passed to TTS even though code blocks are intended to be filtered.
reproduction: Call TTSProcessor._process_chunk with a ChunkEvent whose content is 'before ```secret``` after' after the processor is already in text mode. The manager receives 'before ', then 'secret', then ' after'.
recommendation: When entering code suppression mid-chunk, consume the opening marker before recursively processing the remainder, or make the suppression branch distinguish an opening fence from a closing fence based on state entered before the current chunk. Add coverage for code fences that start and end inside the same chunk and for fences that start mid-chunk.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were included for this feature, and the shown implementation has no in-file assertions covering mid-chunk code fence transitions.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a processor unit test with a fake TTSManager/SpeechService asserting that 'hello ```print(secret)``` world' only sends 'hello ' and ' world' to TTS.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/api/processing/tts/processor.py code-marker transition logic plus focused TTSProcessor tests.
